<span data-as="p">CodeRabbit learnings are flexible, natural-language statements about code-review preferences whose purpose can include the following:</span>
<ul>
<li>Special instructions about reviewing particular files.</li>
<li>Guidance for reviewing all of the files of one repository.</li>
<li>Code-review preferences that CodeRabbit must apply across all of your organization’s repositories.</li>
</ul>
<div data-as="iframe" class="flex justify-center w-full"><div class="object-contain w-full mint-w-full mint-aspect-video mint-rounded-xl" style="aspect-ratio:16/9"></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Every time CodeRabbit prepares to add a comment to a pull request or issue, it loads the learnings that apply based on your <a href="#specify-the-scope-of-learnings" class="link">configured scope</a>. Depending on your settings, CodeRabbit applies either the repository’s learnings only, or all of your organization’s learnings. CodeRabbit uses these learnings as additional context or instructions for its comment.</span>
<span data-as="p">Learnings created from an open pull request first apply only to that source pull request. A learning tied to a filename pattern becomes eligible when that pattern matches a changed file. CodeRabbit then evaluates the learning against the changed code and applies it only when it is relevant to that change. Relevant path matches retain priority when CodeRabbit selects which relevant learnings to apply.</span>
<span data-as="p">Filename-pattern matching is consistent across common path formats: patterns match paths with or without leading <code>./</code> or <code>/</code> prefixes, paths that use Windows-style separators, and files whose names start with a dot. This behavior requires no configuration change or customer action.</span>
<span data-as="p">Use learnings for incremental preferences that emerge during code reviews—preferences that don’t require a formal configuration change but should be applied to future reviews. Use <a href="/configuration/path-instructions" class="link">review instructions</a> or coding guidelines for formal, documented standards.</span>
<span data-as="p">You can review and edit your organization’s CodeRabbit learnings at any time, as detailed later in this page.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="add-learnings" aria-labelledby="_R_n5deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#add-learnings" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Add learnings">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_n5deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Add learnings</span></h2>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="adding-a-learning-via-comment" aria-labelledby="_R_p5deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#adding-a-learning-via-comment" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Adding a learning via comment">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_p5deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Adding a learning via comment</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">To add learnings to the database CodeRabbit keeps about your organization’s preferences, communicate your preferences using natural language, in a comment attached to any pull request or issue.</span>
<span data-as="p">If CodeRabbit decides to create one or more learnings based on a comment, then it makes this explicit in its response to that comment by adding a collapsible section titled <strong>Learnings Added</strong> to its own response comment.</span>
<span data-as="p">Imagine a scenario where CodeRabbit has reviewed a GitHub-based pull request from your team that adds a feature to an authentication middleware library. CodeRabbit has flagged a certain file as needing improvement, attaching this comment to the relevant lines in its review:</span>
<blockquote>
<span data-as="p">Consider using nested try-catch blocks here to handle different error scenarios more comprehensively.</span>
</blockquote>
<span data-as="p">If this critique disagrees with your team’s coding practices specific to try-catch blocks, then you can reply to this CodeRabbit comment using a comment of your own, addressed to the <code>@coderabbitai</code> service account on GitHub:</span>
<blockquote>
<span data-as="p">@coderabbitai Actually, we’ve found that nested try-catch blocks make our auth middleware harder to debug in production. We prefer early returns with specific error codes - it’s cleaner and our monitoring tools can track them better.</span>
</blockquote>
<span data-as="p">CodeRabbit considers your reply, and decides to make a learning out of it. It acknowledges this in another reply:</span>
<blockquote>
<span data-as="p">You’re absolutely right about the debugging benefits. Early returns with specific error codes do provide better clarity and monitoring capabilities. I’ll remember this preference for your authentication middleware. Thank you for the guidance!</span>
</blockquote>
<span data-as="p">CodeRabbit also adds a <strong>Learnings added</strong> section to this comment, making explicit the fact that this chat has modified its future behavior with your team.</span>
<span data-as="p">CodeRabbit then creates a new learnings record for itself. Along with metadata such as the pull request number, filename, and GitHub user associated with the learning, CodeRabbit adds this self-instructive text to the new record:</span>
<blockquote>
<span data-as="p">In authentication middleware, prefer returning early with specific error codes rather than nested try-catch blocks. This improves readability and makes error tracking easier in production environments.</span>
</blockquote>
<span data-as="p">If your organization requires approval before newly created chat-sourced learnings are applied, CodeRabbit creates a pending request instead of immediately adding the learning to the active learning set. Admins can approve or disapprove the request from the Learnings dashboard, and pending requests auto-approve after the configured delay unless an admin rejects them first. Existing learnings are not affected. On CodeRabbit SaaS, CodeRabbit-inferred Learnings created automatically by the review pipeline continue to apply immediately to their source pull request, and remain withheld from other pull requests until the source pull request merges.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="add-learnings-from-files" aria-labelledby="_R_1j5deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#add-learnings-from-files" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Add learnings from files">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_1j5deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Add learnings from files</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">You can import content from any file in your repository as learnings. This is useful for converting existing team documentation into learnings that CodeRabbit will apply during reviews.</span>
<span data-as="p">To import a file as learnings, mention the file in a pull request comment:</span>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="credential-redaction" aria-labelledby="_R_215deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#credential-redaction" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Credential redaction">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_215deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Credential redaction</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">When a learning is newly created during PR Review, imported, approved, or edited by an administrator, CodeRabbit replaces recognizable credentials with credential-type markers before storing the text and creating its vector embedding. Markers identify the credential type, for example, <code>***REDACTED_GITHUB_TOKEN***</code>, <code>***REDACTED_STRIPE_KEY***</code>, or <code>***REDACTED_URI_PASSWORD***</code>. For each connection URI, CodeRabbit removes only the password; the scheme, username, host, port, and path remain.</span>
<span data-as="p">CodeRabbit later reuses the same redacted text in PR Review context and CSV exports. Ordinary guidance and code examples that discuss authentication without containing a high-confidence secret remain unchanged. Redaction occurs only at write time and does not backfill or clean previously stored learnings.</span>

<span data-as="p">When communicating with CodeRabbit during an active code review, follow these practices to create effective learnings:</span>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="consider-if-it’s-a-pattern-or-a-one-off" aria-labelledby="_R_2b5deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#consider-if-it’s-a-pattern-or-a-one-off" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Consider if it’s a pattern or a one-off">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_2b5deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Consider if it’s a pattern or a one-off</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">Determine whether a correction represents a team-wide preference that should apply to all future reviews, or a situation specific to this pull request.</span>
<span data-as="p">Not every correction should become a learning. For one-time exceptions, such as unusual temporary code patterns during a migration, resolve the comment without creating a learning. For systemic preferences that should persist across reviews, provide feedback that CodeRabbit can store as a learning.</span>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="kpi-cards" aria-labelledby="_R_355deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#kpi-cards" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: KPI cards">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_355deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">KPI cards</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">At the top of the dashboard, four KPI (Key Performance Indicator) cards summarize the state of your learnings. Clicking a card filters and sorts the table to the relevant subset.</span>
<!-- --><div role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]"><div data-id="base-ui-_R_395deehkd74t9_-viewport" tabindex="-1" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" style="overflow:scroll" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" role="region" aria-label="Scrollable table"><div role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" class="flex"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&_th]:text-left [&_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums [&_td]:min-w-[150px]"><thead><tr><th>Card</th><th>What it shows</th><th>Click behavior</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Total Learnings</strong></td><td>The total number of learnings stored for your organization.</td><td>Shows all learnings, sorted by <strong>Last Used</strong> descending.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Active</strong></td><td>Learnings that have been used in a review within the last 30 days.</td><td>Filters to active learnings only, sorted by <strong>Last Used</strong> descending.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Never Used</strong></td><td>Learnings that have never been applied to a review (usage count of 0).</td><td>Filters to never-used learnings, sorted by <strong>Created At</strong> descending.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Created This Week</strong></td><td>Learnings created within the last 7 days.</td><td>Filters to recently created learnings, sorted by <strong>Created At</strong> descending.</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Use these cards to quickly identify which learnings are actively influencing reviews, which ones might be stale, and what your team has added recently.</span>

<span data-as="p">The learnings table contains the following columns:</span>
<!-- --><div role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]"><div data-id="base-ui-_R_3h5deehkd74t9_-viewport" tabindex="-1" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" style="overflow:scroll" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" role="region" aria-label="Scrollable table"><div role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" class="flex"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&_th]:text-left [&_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums [&_td]:min-w-[150px]"><thead><tr><th>Column</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Learning</strong></td><td>The natural-language text of the learning (the description).</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Usage</strong></td><td>The number of times CodeRabbit has applied this learning during reviews and chat sessions.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Last Used</strong></td><td>The date this learning was most recently applied to a review or chat session.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Created At</strong></td><td>The date this learning was created.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Updated At</strong></td><td>The date this learning was last modified.</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="view-learning-details" aria-labelledby="_R_3j5deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#view-learning-details" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: View learning details">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_3j5deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">View learning details</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Click any row in the table, or click the <strong>Action</strong> button on the row, to open a detailed view of that learning. The detail view displays the following fields:</span>
<!-- --><div role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]"><div data-id="base-ui-_R_3n5deehkd74t9_-viewport" tabindex="-1" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" style="overflow:scroll" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" role="region" aria-label="Scrollable table"><div role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" class="flex"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&_th]:text-left [&_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums [&_td]:min-w-[150px]"><thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Description</strong></td><td>The full text of the learning. Recognized credentials appear as <a href="#credential-redaction" class="link">redaction markers</a>.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Usage</strong></td><td>The number of times CodeRabbit has applied this learning during reviews and chat sessions.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Created by</strong></td><td>The username of the person whose comment created the learning.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Repository</strong></td><td>The repository the learning is associated with.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Created at</strong></td><td>The date this learning was created.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Updated at</strong></td><td>The date this learning was last modified.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Last used</strong></td><td>The date this learning was most recently applied.</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">From this view you can also edit the description or delete the learning.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="review-pending-learnings" aria-labelledby="_R_3r5deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#review-pending-learnings" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Review pending learnings">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_3r5deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Review pending learnings</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Organizations that require approval for newly created chat-sourced learnings have a <strong>Pending approvals</strong> tab on the Learnings dashboard. This tab lists new learnings waiting for review, including the requested learning text, source repository, source pull request when available, requester, request date, and auto-approval deadline. CodeRabbit applies <a href="#credential-redaction" class="link">credential redaction</a> again before storing approved text.</span>
<span data-as="p">Administrators can approve or disapprove pending learnings. You can act on a single pending learning or select multiple rows for bulk approval or disapproval.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sort-learnings" aria-labelledby="_R_415deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#sort-learnings" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Sort learnings">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_415deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Sort learnings</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">You can sort the table by any column. Click a column header to sort by that column in ascending order, and click it again to switch to descending order. Sorting lets you quickly find your most-used learnings, your oldest learnings, or the ones most recently updated.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="filter-displayed-learnings" aria-labelledby="_R_455deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#filter-displayed-learnings" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Filter displayed learnings">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_455deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Filter displayed learnings</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Over time, the learnings that CodeRabbit gathers for your organization can become quite numerous. This can make manually browsing the full list difficult. The CodeRabbit web interface has search and filtering tools to help you find specific learnings, based on the topic of the learning text, or on other metadata.</span>
<span data-as="p">To filter the displayed learnings by topic or concept, enter that topic or concept into the <strong>Search learnings</strong> field. Because this is a vector-based similarity search, the returned learnings don’t necessarily contain the exact text of your search terms.</span>
<span data-as="p">For example, to see the top learnings that have to do with error reporting, enter <code>error reporting</code> into <strong>Search learnings</strong>. This will find learnings about exceptions, try-catch, error codes, and other semantically related topics.</span>
<span data-as="p">To filter the displayed learnings by repository, file path, or user, click the <strong>Filters</strong> button at the top right of the table and select additional criteria. Your repositories, file paths, and users will automatically populate as tags when you search the values.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="edit-or-delete-learnings" aria-labelledby="_R_4f5deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#edit-or-delete-learnings" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Edit or delete learnings">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_4f5deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Edit or delete learnings</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">You can edit and delete learnings in three ways:</span>
<span data-as="p"><strong>Via the web interface</strong>: If your account has the <strong>Admin</strong> <a href="/management/roles" class="link">CodeRabbit role</a> with your organization, then you can edit the text of any stored learning or delete it through the CodeRabbit dashboard. When you save an edit, CodeRabbit applies <a href="#credential-redaction" class="link">credential redaction</a> again before storing the updated text.</span>
<span data-as="p">To edit or delete a learning via the web interface:</span>
<ol>
<li>
<span data-as="p">Click the <strong>Action</strong> button on the learning’s row in the table, which resembles a right arrow.</span>
</li>
<li>
<span data-as="p">Edit the <strong>Description</strong> to edit the learning, or press <strong>Delete</strong> to delete it.</span>
</li>
</ol>
<span data-as="p"><strong>Via CodeRabbit comments</strong>: Any user can request learning modifications through natural language comments in pull requests or issues. Ask CodeRabbit to remove or modify specific learnings by mentioning <code>@coderabbitai</code> and describing the change you want.</span>
<span data-as="p"><strong>Via the public API</strong>: Enterprise teams can <a href="/api-reference/learnings-update" class="link">update</a> or <a href="/api-reference/learnings-delete" class="link">delete</a> Learnings programmatically. Deletion is idempotent, so retrying the same request is safe.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="export-and-transfer-learnings" aria-labelledby="_R_4t5deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#export-and-transfer-learnings" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Export and transfer learnings">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_4t5deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Export and transfer learnings</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">You can export your organization’s learnings and import them into another CodeRabbit account. This is useful when migrating accounts or consolidating organizations.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="export-learnings" aria-labelledby="_R_515deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#export-learnings" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Export learnings">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_515deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Export learnings</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">To export your learnings:</span>
<ol>
<li>Visit <a href="https://app.coderabbit.ai" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" class="link">the CodeRabbit web interface</a>.</li>
<li>Navigate to <strong>Learnings</strong> in the sidebar.</li>
<li>Click the export option to download your learnings as a CSV file.</li>
</ol>
<span data-as="p">The CSV file contains all your learnings with their associated metadata, including the repository, file path, usage count, last date edited, last date used, date created, and learning text. Exported learning text reflects any applied <a href="#credential-redaction" class="link">redaction markers</a> rather than the original secrets.</span>
<span data-as="p">The <a href="/api-reference/learnings-list" class="link">Learnings API</a> provides programmatic JSON and CSV export. Filter exports with case-insensitive text search, up to 10 exact file paths, or usage states for Learnings used in the last 30 days, never used, or created in the last 7 days.</span>
<span data-as="p">User and workspace API keys can update and delete Learnings; legacy organization API keys and agentic API keys cannot. Workspace keys must select one organization for each write. CodeRabbit redacts recognized credentials before storage, and deletion is idempotent. Learnings write requests share a limit of 10 requests per minute per organization.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="import-learnings-to-a-new-account" aria-labelledby="_R_5d5deehkd74t9_"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#import-learnings-to-a-new-account" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header: Import learnings to a new account">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="18" height="18" stroke-width="2" class="size-3 shrink-0"><use href="#mi-mint-1-Link"></use></svg></div></a></div><span id="_R_5d5deehkd74t9_" class="cursor-pointer">Import learnings to a new account</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">To import learnings into a new CodeRabbit account:</span>
<ol>
<li>
<span data-as="p">Ensure the new account is connected to your repository and has an active CodeRabbit subscription.</span>
</li>
<li>
<span data-as="p">Add the exported learnings CSV file to a branch in your repository.</span>
</li>
<li>
<span data-as="p">Create a pull request from that branch.</span>
</li>
<li>
<span data-as="p">Use CodeRabbit chat to request the import:</span>

<span data-as="p">The <a href="/reference/configuration#param-knowledge-base-learnings-scope" class="link"><code>knowledge_base.learnings.scope</code></a> setting lets you specify the <em>scope</em> that CodeRabbit applies to all of the learnings it has collected about your organization. With the default, <code>auto</code>, CodeRabbit applies only a public repository’s own learnings and applies all of your organization’s learnings when reviewing a private repository. With <code>global</code>, it applies all of your organization’s learnings to all code reviews. With <code>local</code>, it applies only the learnings associated with the repository being reviewed.</span>

<!-- -->
<span data-as="p">On CodeRabbit SaaS, a Learning created while a pull request is open remains available only to that source pull request and is withheld from reviews of other pull requests. When Learnings retrieval is available, the source pull request can retrieve its 20 most recent source-scoped Learnings.</span>
<span data-as="p">After the source pull request merges into any branch, its Learnings become available repository-wide and enter normal retrieval. Closing the source pull request without merging keeps its Learnings scoped to that pull request.</span>
<span data-as="p">Approval and dashboard editing continue to work for source-scoped Learnings. See <a href="#review-pending-learnings" class="link">Review pending learnings</a> and <a href="#edit-or-delete-learnings" class="link">Edit or delete learnings</a>.</span>

<span data-as="p">If CodeRabbit seems to ignore your learnings—for example, continuing to make suggestions that contradict existing learnings—try this workaround:</span>
<ol>
<li>
<span data-as="p"><strong>Review existing learnings.</strong> Go to your project’s Learnings page and verify that all relevant learnings are active and clearly phrased.</span>

<li>
<span data-as="p">Consider possible conflicts with path instructions or coding guidelines. Path instructions precede learnings.</span>

<span data-as="p">Team conventions evolve, and learnings can become stale. To maintain learnings effectively:</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Quarterly review.</strong> Set a reminder to review your learnings every quarter. Look for learnings that reference deprecated patterns, old file structures, or outdated team decisions.</li>
<li><strong>Delete contradictory learnings.</strong> If you find learnings that conflict with current practices, delete them to avoid confusing CodeRabbit.</li>
<li><strong>Update rather than accumulate.</strong> When team standards change, update or delete old learnings rather than adding new ones that contradict them. Multiple conflicting learnings on the same topic can produce inconsistent behavior.</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">To identify outdated learnings:</span>
<ol>
<li>Use the similarity search to find learnings about areas where your practices have changed.</li>
<li>Filter by creation date to find the oldest learnings.</li>
<li>Review learnings from team members who are no longer active.</li>
